I haven't had any times where I felt like my old self or wanted to work on my fishing boat or guitars again. Even during the times when some of the other strange things in my head eased up a bit, that heavy, empty feeling never really left.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about these 'other strange things' in your head that you mentioned eased up a bit at times, what were they and how did they change over the past two years?\n\nPatient: I keep hearing this man's voice behind me telling me I'm dangerous and going to kill someone, and I've been convinced my company bugged my badge and the forklifts to track me. These things have been going on for over a year and a half now, and they don't always match how down I'm feeling. Even last year, during a brief time when my mood lifted a bit and I didn't feel quite as deeply crushed, those voices and the feeling of being watched never stopped.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how the voice behind you and the beliefs about being tracked relate to your feelings of emptiness and lack of motivation, or do they seem like separate issues to you?\n\nPatient: They feel closely linked to me, like they've been happening side by side. Around the same time I lost interest in my hobbies and felt so empty, the voice got louder and I became convinced they were tracking my badge. The hopelessness and those strange things in my head just seemed to hit me during the exact same stretch.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear and your beliefs about being tracked are real, or do you ever question whether they might be a product of your own mind?\n\nPatient: They feel completely real to me, and I just can't shake them off. Even though my wife tells me it's not real and that I'm being crazy, I truly believe the company is tracking my badge and that the voice is actually speaking to me.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any times or situations where you questioned the reality of the voice or the tracking, or have you always been completely convinced of their reality?\n\nPatient: I’ve almost always been completely convinced they are real, and I haven't really been able to doubt it. Even though my wife constantly tells me it's crazy, the voice sounds like it's right behind me and the tracking feels so targeted. It just feels too real to be anything else.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever acted on the instructions or warnings from the voice, or taken any specific actions to try and evade the tracking you believe is happening?\n\nPatient: When the voice tells me I'm going to kill someone, I get so terrified of causing an accident that I often freeze up or just step away from my forklift mid-shift. As for the tracking, I haven't tried to destroy the badge or the devices because I'm too afraid of getting fired on the spot, but I constantly worry about them and feel watched. It's just exhausting trying to get through the day like this.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other types of hallucinations, such as seeing things that aren't there, in addition to hearing the voice behind you?\n\nPatient: No, I don't see things that aren't there. It's strictly that man's voice I hear right behind me, telling me that I'm dangerous and going to kill someone.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any beliefs that you were somehow special, famous, or had special powers, in addition to the beliefs about being tracked and the voice telling you you're dangerous?\n\nPatient: No, I’ve never thought I was special, famous, or had any kind of special powers. My mind is really just focused on being tracked by the company and the constant fear that I'm a danger to the people around me.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any periods where the voice told you to do something specific, other than warning you about being dangerous, or have the delusions about being tracked led you to behave in ways that significantly impacted your daily life or relationships?\n\nPatient: No, the voice never commands me to do specific things; it just repeats those critical comments calling me dangerous and saying I'm going to kill someone. But the tracking has really impacted my life because it makes me step away from my forklift mid-shift, and it causes a lot of tension with my wife since she keeps telling me it's crazy, which just makes me isolate myself even more.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any times when the voice or your beliefs about being tracked seemed to directly influence your lack of motivation or interest in activities, or were there other factors at play that you think contributed to your apathy?\n\nPatient: It feels like they are completely tangled together because they started at the exact same time. Just as the voice got louder and I became convinced they were tracking me, I also lost all interest in my projects and felt completely hopeless. The heavy, depressed feeling and the strange things in my head have just been running side-by-side, dragging me down together.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant changes in the intensity or frequency of the voice or your beliefs about being tracked over the past two years, or have they remained relatively consistent?\n\nPatient: They have been a pretty steady, ongoing problem for well over a year and a half now. While there are times when they ease up just a little bit, they are generally very consistent and remained present even during a stretch last year when my mood felt slightly better.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if the voice you hear and the beliefs about being tracked are present even when you're not feeling particularly down or empty, or do they tend to worsen when your depressive symptoms are more pronounced?\n\nPatient: Yes, they are definitely still there even when my mood temporarily gets a little better. There was a stretch last year where I wasn't feeling quite as deeply low or crushed, but I was still convinced my work badge was bugged and kept hearing that man's voice telling me I was dangerous.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice and the feelings of being tracked would still be present if you were able to regain your interest in hobbies and feel joyful again, or are they somehow linked to your current state of mind?\n\nPatient: I honestly think they would still be there, because they seem to have a life of their own. Even during that stretch last year when my mood lifted a bit and I felt less crushed, the voice and the tracking didn't go away at all. It just feels like they persist even when the heavy sadness lets up a little.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced any periods where the voice stopped or significantly reduced, and if so, did your beliefs about being tracked change during those times?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really had any periods where the voice stopped or went away. For well over a year and a half now, both the voice and the tracking have just been a steady, constant presence without any real break. It's incredibly exhausting because they just never seem to let up.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced any physical sensations or feelings that you believe are a direct result of the tracking devices or the voice's influence?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really felt any physical sensations or bodily feelings from the tracking devices or the voice. It's really just the mental stress of hearing those things and constantly worrying about being watched.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your lack of interest in activities and feelings of emptiness would improve if the voice and the beliefs about being tracked were to stop, or do you feel like they are separate issues?\n\nPatient: I feel like they are somewhat separate issues, honestly. Even before the voices and tracking thoughts became really prominent, I already felt worn down and completely joyless. And even when those strange thoughts and voices have eased up a bit at times, this heavy, depressed feeling and lack of interest have just persisted and never really let up.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned that the voice and the beliefs about being tracked started around the same time you lost interest in your hobbies and felt empty, but did the depressive feelings of emptiness and lack of motivation precede the onset of the voice and tracking beliefs, or did they start simultaneously?\n\nPatient: Looking back, the heavy, depressed feelings and lack of motivation definitely started first, shortly after the restructuring at work about two years ago. The voice and the tracking beliefs didn't actually develop until a bit later, around a year and a half ago. So that gray, empty feeling was already weighing me down before the other things even started.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned that the depressive feelings started before the voice and tracking beliefs, can you estimate how long the depressive symptoms were present before the psychotic symptoms began?\n\nPatient: The heavy, joyless feelings and losing interest in my hobbies started shortly after the restructuring, which has been going on for a little over two years now. The voices and the tracking beliefs didn't become a steady problem until about a year and a half ago. So, I'd estimate there was a gap of about six to nine months where I was just deeply depressed before those other things actually started.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm that the feelings of emptiness and lack of motivation started about six to nine months before the voice and tracking beliefs began, and have these depressive symptoms persisted even when the intensity of the voice and tracking beliefs may have varied?\n\nPatient: Yes, that's correct—the feelings of emptiness and lack of motivation definitely started about six months before the voices and tracking beliefs began. And yes, those depressed feelings have remained constant and heavy, never really letting up even during times when the voices and tracking thoughts became less intense or eased up a bit.\n\nDoctor: Can you further clarify if there were any significant events or stressors that occurred during the six to nine months before the voice and tracking beliefs started, which might have contributed to the onset of your depressive symptoms?\n\nPatient: Yes, about three years ago, my long-time employer underwent a major restructuring where they brought in automation, cut my hours, and pressured older workers like me to retire. It felt like a direct threat to my identity and future, which made me withdraw and lose all interest in my hobbies months before the voices and tracking beliefs ever started.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any significant changes in your behavior or daily functioning during the six to nine months before the voice and tracking beliefs started, and how they might have differed from your behavior after these symptoms began?\n\nPatient: During those first months, I withdrew from everything—I stopped going to choir, abandoned my woodworking, and kept to myself at work out of deep depression and guilt. Once the voices and tracking beliefs started, it added intense fear and paranoia on top of that sadness, making me freeze up on the job and isolate myself even more. Before that, I was just deeply empty, but afterward, I became constantly terrified.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned that the depressive feelings started before the voice and tracking beliefs, can you confirm if the depressive symptoms have always been present whenever the psychotic symptoms were present, or have there been times when you experienced the voice and tracking beliefs without feeling depressed?"

Yes, there was a stretch last year when my mood improved a bit and I didn't feel as deeply low or crushed. Even during those weeks when the depression eased up, I still heard that man's voice calling me dangerous and remained convinced my work badge was bugged.

The hopelessness and those strange things in my head just seemed to hit me during the exact same stretch.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear and your beliefs about being tracked are real, or do you ever question whether they might be a product of your own mind?\n\nPatient: They feel completely real to me, and I just can't shake them off. Even though my wife tells me it's not real and that I'm being crazy, I truly believe the company is tracking my badge and that the voice is actually speaking to me.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any times or situations where you questioned the reality of the voice or the tracking, or have you always been completely convinced of their reality?\n\nPatient: I’ve almost always been completely convinced they are real, and I haven't really been able to doubt it. Even though my wife constantly tells me it's crazy, the voice sounds like it's right behind me and the tracking feels so targeted. It just feels too real to be anything else.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever acted on the instructions or warnings from the voice, or taken any specific actions to try and evade the tracking you believe is happening?\n\nPatient: When the voice tells me I'm going to kill someone, I get so terrified of causing an accident that I often freeze up or just step away from my forklift mid-shift. As for the tracking, I haven't tried to destroy the badge or the devices because I'm too afraid of getting fired on the spot, but I constantly worry about them and feel watched. It's just exhausting trying to get through the day like this.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other types of hallucinations, such as seeing things that aren't there, in addition to hearing the voice behind you?\n\nPatient: No, I don't see things that aren't there. It's strictly that man's voice I hear right behind me, telling me that I'm dangerous and going to kill someone.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any beliefs that you were somehow special, famous, or had special powers, in addition to the beliefs about being tracked and the voice telling you you're dangerous?\n\nPatient: No, I’ve never thought I was special, famous, or had any kind of special powers. My mind is really just focused on being tracked by the company and the constant fear that I'm a danger to the people around me.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any periods where the voice told you to do something specific, other than warning you about being dangerous, or have the delusions about being tracked led you to behave in ways that significantly impacted your daily life or relationships?\n\nPatient: No, the voice never commands me to do specific things; it just repeats those critical comments calling me dangerous and saying I'm going to kill someone. There was a stretch last year where I wasn't feeling quite as deeply low or crushed, but I was still convinced my work badge was bugged and kept hearing that man's voice telling me I was dangerous.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice and the feelings of being tracked would still be present if you were able to regain your interest in hobbies and feel joyful again, or are they somehow linked to your current state of mind?\n\nPatient: I honestly think they would still be there, because they seem to have a life of their own. The voices and the tracking beliefs didn't become a steady problem until about a year and a half ago. My mind is really just focused on being tracked by the company and the constant fear that I'm a danger to the people around me.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any periods where the voice told you to do something specific, other than warning you about being dangerous, or have the delusions about being tracked led you to behave in ways that significantly impacted your daily life or relationships?\n\nPatient: No, the voice never commands me to do specific things; it just repeats those critical comments calling me dangerous and saying I'm going to kill someone. There was a stretch last year where I wasn't feeling quite as deeply low or crushed, but I was still convinced my work badge was bugged and kept hearing that man's voice telling me I was dangerous.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice and the feelings of being tracked would still be present if you were able to regain your interest in hobbies and feel joyful again, or are they somehow linked to your current state of mind?\n\nPatient: I honestly think they would still be there, because they seem to have a life of their own.
